record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Connect perturbative renormalization results for interacting surfaces, such as surfaces interacting with a single impurity, to a constructive analysis.

evidence.quote: There are also perturbative results on the renormalization surfaces interacting e.g. with a single impurity [DDG] which one would like to connect to a constructive analysis.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a continuous model of a D-dimensional elastic (polymerized) manifold fluctuating in d-dimensional Euclidean space and interacting with a single point-like impurity via a delta-function potential of coupling g (attractive or repulsive). For 0 < D < 2, the perturbative expansion of correlation functions is UV finite for d < d*, where d* = 2D/(2 - D), and develops UV divergences as poles at d = d*. Perturbative renormalizability has been established to all orders by means of a Zimmermann-type forest subtraction operator that renormalizes the impurity coupling constant, yielding a Wilson function, an ε-expansion around d*, and (in the attractive case) non-trivial critical exponents associated with a delocalization transition.

Problem. Provide a fully constructive (non-perturbative) analysis of this model of an interacting D-dimensional manifold coupled to a single impurity. Concretely:

(a) Construct the renormalized correlation functions of the model at d = d* (or in the ε-expansion regime) as the Borel sum, or another rigorously defined resummation, of the perturbative renormalized series, and prove convergence/Borel-summability of the resulting series uniformly in the UV cutoff.

(b) Establish, by constructive methods (e.g., multiscale cluster or loop-vertex expansions adapted to manifold field theories), the existence of the continuum limit of the renormalized model and the existence of a non-Gaussian renormalization-group fixed point in a neighborhood of d = d*, beyond the hierarchical approximation in which such results are already known.

(c) Derive rigorous scaling laws and critical exponents for the localization/delocalization transition that match the perturbative predictions.
artifact.status_search_result: Perturbative renormalizability of D-dimensional manifolds interacting with a single delta impurity has been proved (David–Duplantier–Guitter), and a hierarchical version admits a rigorous constructive analysis with a non-Gaussian fixed point for 1 ≤ D < 2 and small ε. However, no full constructive (non-hierarchical) treatment of the continuum model appears in the literature, so the problem of connecting the perturbative renormalization of interacting surfaces/manifolds with impurities to a constructive analysis remains open.

status_evidence.title: Renormalization Theory for Interacting Crumpled Manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Perturbative renormalizability is proven to all orders by constructing a subtraction operator based on a generalization of the Zimmermann forests formalism, making the theory finite at d=d*.
status_evidence.claim: Perturbative renormalization of D-dimensional manifolds interacting with a single delta impurity is established.

status_evidence.title: Renormalization Group Approach to Interacting Crumpled Surfaces: The hierarchical recursion
status_evidence.snippet: For a hierarchical version of the model, rigorous existence of the scaling limit and convergence to a non-Gaussian fixed point is proven for 1 ≤ D < 2 and ε > 0 sufficiently small.
status_evidence.claim: Only the hierarchical version has a rigorous constructive treatment; the full continuum constructive problem remains.
